title: New Castle, Henry County Seat
summary: New Castle has been the seat of Henry County since the county was cut from Shelby County in 1798 and named for Patrick Henry.
bodyMarkdown:
New Castle is a small town with an old job. Since 1798 it has been the seat of Henry County, in the rolling farm country between Louisville, Frankfort, and Cincinnati.

The county came first. On December 14, 1798, the General Assembly [cut Henry County from Shelby County](https://grokipedia.com/page/Henry_County,_Kentucky) and named it for [Patrick Henry](/people/#patrick-henry), the Virginia orator of "give me liberty or give me death." Kentucky had been part of Virginia only six years earlier, and many of its new counties took Virginia names.

The land had drawn people long before the county lines. Salt springs pulled hunters and surveyors here in the 1770s. In July 1773 [Jacob Drennon](/people/#jacob-drennon) and [Matthew Bracken](/people/#matthew-bracken) claimed the lick that still carries Drennon's name, in what became the county's southern edge. The story of that salt works is told at [Drennon Springs](/stories/drennon-springs-salt-works/).

New Castle grew around a courthouse square. The dates for the town itself vary. Kentucky Land Office records give 1817 as its establishment. Some histories call that its incorporation, while others date incorporation to 1851.

The farms around it raised tobacco, hay, and cattle for generations. Tobacco has faded, but livestock and hay still matter, and the square still anchors the town.

New Castle also produced a congressman with a grim place in history. William Jordan Graves, born here in 1805, served as a Whig in Congress. In 1838 he killed Maine congressman Jonathan Cilley in a duel, and the outcry helped lead Congress to outlaw dueling in the District of Columbia.

After the Civil War, Black residents built their own institutions. Washington Lodge #1513 of the Grand United Order of Odd Fellows, an African American fraternal order, was founded in New Castle in 1872 by formerly enslaved men. Black children attended the New Castle Colored School until integration.

The 1863 Caplinger House, built by druggist James N. Caplinger, served for years as the Henry County History Center. It was sold in 2017 and is now a private home.

To the south, Henry County meets [Shelbyville](/stories/shelbyville/) and Shelby County, the parent county it was cut from.

## Kentucky today

The Henry County Courthouse still stands on the square in New Castle, on Main Street (US 421). A state historical marker by the lodge building tells the story of the Odd Fellows lodge. Please treat the Caplinger House as a private residence.
